messages.text: Sunday, November 15 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies, clarinet recitals, and the quiet drift of herbicide

A cool, grey Saturday in Canton brings a focus on musical performance and local environmental research. We look at the subtle ways chemicals reshape our fields and how regional management is changing the way we live alongside deer.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 44 degrees and a low around 31 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:25 AM and sets at 5:12 PM, with the moon currently in a waxing crescent phase at 29.3 percent illumination.
Musical afternoons in Ann Arbor
Graduate student Jaden Tan performs a clarinet recital at 2 PM at the Earl V. Moore Building, followed by the Student Composer Concert Series at 7 PM in the same venue.
A community meeting is scheduled for November 18 at 6:30 PM.
Regional shifts in deer management

Southern Michigan communities are increasingly moving toward regional management strategies to mitigate deer-related traffic accidents and protect local biodiversity. These collaborative efforts aim to address population growth through shared resources rather than isolated municipal actions.

Monday, November 16 · Canton, Michigan
Tuba resonance in Ann Arbor and the quiet drift of herbicide research

An overcast Sunday brings a cool, steady temperature perfect for indoor academic seminars or evening recitals. Local attention turns to the intersection of environmental impact studies and regional legal developments.
Expect overcast skies throughout the day with a high near 50 degrees and a low of 35 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:26 AM and sets at 5:11 PM, with the moon currently in its first-quarter phase at 38.3 percent illumination.
Academic and musical rhythms
Consider the lecture on boundary stratifications of Hurwitz spaces at East Hall at 4:00 PM. Later, Jake Alford performs a tuba recital at the Walgreen Drama Center at 8:00 PM.
A community meeting is scheduled for November 18 at 6:30 PM.
Legal filings and environmental research

Osama Siblani has filed a defamation lawsuit against former U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Wayne County Circuit Court. Meanwhile, University of Michigan research highlights that low doses of the herbicide dicamba cause wood sorrel to produce smaller, more numerous flowers.
